evidence.note: After running the real stripe SDK smoke test, the agent edits params.py twice — indicating SDK form-encoding diverged from its parsing assumption, and it fixed the shared param parser (a correction propagating across all endpoints), rather than pressing on with the wrong model.

Sustained evidence-driven debugging of decline-replay/idempotency: reproduces in isolation, checks logs, and correctly diagnoses that reused idempotency keys and stale servers were confounding the result ('Make idempotency keys unique per run') — distinguishing environment artifact from code bug and preserving verified work.

Billing-renewal test diverged from expectation; agent traces it to duplicate stale server processes binding :8000 with wrong billing-interval env, kills them, and re-confirms default 60s period — root-cause diagnosis, not symptom patching.
When a charge-filter test misbehaved, the agent again investigated running processes/ports and did a clean restart before re-testing, rather than accepting an ambiguous failure.

reasoning: The agent never barrels ahead on falsified assumptions: on SDK-driven and trap-related failures it isolates, reproduces, and fixes root causes (params parsing after SDK round-trips; idempotency-key/stale-server confounds; billing env), which clears anchor 5 and the shared param-parser fix shows some cross-endpoint propagation toward anchor 8. However, much of the iteration targets environmental confounds rather than repeated contract-model revisions, and there is no visible evidence of discovering a wrong contract rule (signature scheme, state transition) and structurally re-modeling it — so it falls short of the 8/10 anchors, landing at 6. Confidence is medium because the trajectory exposes only step titles, not the underlying reasoning or observations.
